question: Four items were placed inside a pitch-black box with a small viewing hole: a glow stick, a silver coin, a flat glass mirror, and a live firefly. Which items can be seen WITHOUT turning on any external torch?
options: Glow stick and firefly only
Silver coin and mirror only
All four items
Glow stick, firefly, and mirror
answer: Glow stick and firefly only

question: A light sensor measured the light passing through three equal-sized sheets placed one by one in front of a 100-unit torch: Sheet P (0 units), Sheet Q (50 units), and Sheet R (100 units). If Sheet Q is placed between Sheet P and Sheet R in a straight line in front of the torch, what shadow appears on the screen behind Sheet R?
options: A dark shadow because Sheet P blocks all light
A faint shadow because Sheet Q lets some light pass
No shadow because Sheet R allows 100 units of light
Two separate shadows on the screen
answer: A dark shadow because Sheet P blocks all light

question: An L-shaped wooden block is held in front of a light source. Depending on how the block is rotated, which shadow shape is IMPOSSIBLE for this block to cast on a flat screen?
options: A circle
A square
A rectangle
An L-shape
answer: A circle

question: Farhan wants to increase the size of a puppet's shadow on a screen without moving the screen itself. What two adjustments can he make?
options: Move torch closer to puppet, or puppet further from screen
Move torch further from puppet, or puppet closer to screen
Move both torch and puppet further from the screen
Move torch closer to screen, and puppet closer to screen
answer: Move torch closer to puppet, or puppet further from screen

question: In an experiment, a torch is placed 50 cm from a screen. An opaque toy is placed at varying distances from the torch: 10 cm away → shadow height 25 cm; 20 cm away → shadow height 15 cm; 30 cm away → shadow height 10 cm. What conclusion can be drawn from this data?
options: Decreasing the distance between light source and object increases shadow size
Increasing the distance between light source and object increases shadow size
Distance between light source and object has no effect on shadow size
Moving the screen further away always decreases shadow size
answer: Decreasing the distance between light source and object increases shadow size

question: An opaque wooden card has two cut-out shapes: a small circle and a small square. A torch shines through the card onto a screen. What pattern will be observed on the screen?
options: A dark rectangle shadow with a bright circle and a bright square
A bright background with a dark circle shadow and a dark square shadow
A completely dark shadow covering the entire screen
Two dark square shadows with bright circle centers
answer: A dark rectangle shadow with a bright circle and a bright square

question: Sheet X is clear glass (transparent), Sheet Y is tracing paper (translucent), and Sheet Z is cardboard (opaque). The three sheets overlap each other partially in front of a torch. Which region of the shadow on the screen will be the DARKEST?
options: The region where Sheet Z is present
The region where Sheet X and Sheet Y overlap
The region where Sheet X alone is present
All regions will have equal darkness
answer: The region where Sheet Z is present

question: Bala sets up three cardboard sheets (A, B, C) in a line, each with a pinhole in the center. A lit candle is at one end and Bala looks through from the other end. What happens if sheet B is shifted 2 cm to the left?
options: Bala cannot see the flame because light travels in straight lines and is blocked by sheet B
Bala can still see the flame because light bends around the shifted pinhole
The flame appears dimmer but stays visible
The shadow of the flame becomes twice as large
answer: Bala cannot see the flame because light travels in straight lines and is blocked by sheet B

question: Two identical torches, T1 and T2, are placed side-by-side pointing at a single opaque water bottle in front of a screen. What will be observed on the screen?
options: Two shadow regions that may partially overlap
Only one single black shadow
No shadow because the light sources cancel each other out
Four separate circular shadows
answer: Two shadow regions that may partially overlap

question: A hollow toilet paper cardboard roll (open at both ends) is held in front of a torch. Which pair of shadow shapes can it form on a screen depending on how it is held?
options: A ring or a rectangle
A solid circle or a triangle
A triangle or a ring
A square or a solid circle
answer: A ring or a rectangle

question: Kai wants to test if the MATERIAL of an object affects the darkness of its shadow. Which set of variables MUST he keep constant to conduct a fair test?
options: Size of object, shape of object, and distances between torch, object, and screen
Type of material, size of object, and brightness of light source
Distance between torch and object, type of material, and screen position
Darkness of shadow, shape of object, and type of material
answer: Size of object, shape of object, and distances between torch, object, and screen

question: A periscope uses two flat mirrors set at angles to let a sailor inside a submarine view objects on the sea surface. How does light travel through the periscope?
options: Light from the ship reflects off the top mirror, then off the bottom mirror into the eye
Light from the eye reflects off the bottom mirror, then off the top mirror to the ship
Light bends continuously inside the tube without touching any mirrors
Light from the ship is absorbed by the top mirror and recreated at the bottom mirror
answer: Light from the ship reflects off the top mirror, then off the bottom mirror into the eye

question: The length of a flagpole's shadow was measured outdoors at four different times: Time W = 4 m, Time X = 0.5 m, Time Y = 2 m, Time Z = 5 m. Which time most likely represents 12:00 noon?
options: Time X
Time W
Time Y
Time Z
answer: Time X

question: Susan stacks identical tracing paper sheets between a torch and a light sensor. 1 sheet: 600 units; 2 sheets: 300 units; 3 sheets: 150 units; 4 sheets: 0 units. What can she conclude about stacking translucent materials?
options: As the number of sheets increases, less light passes through until it becomes opaque
Adding more sheets increases the amount of light reaching the sensor
Tracing paper becomes transparent when 4 sheets are stacked
The thickness of tracing paper has no effect on light transmission
answer: As the number of sheets increases, less light passes through until it becomes opaque

question: A vertical stick is placed on open ground under the Sun in Singapore. From 8:00 am to 12:00 noon, how do the LENGTH and POSITION of the stick's shadow change?
options: Shadow length decreases, and shadow position moves from west towards south/middle
Shadow length increases, and shadow position moves from east to west
Shadow length remains constant, and shadow position moves from north to south
Shadow length decreases, and shadow position moves from east to west
answer: Shadow length decreases, and shadow position moves from west towards south/middle

question: A cat sits inside a completely pitch-black room containing a large glass mirror. Can the cat see its own reflection in the mirror?
options: No, because there is no light source to reflect off the cat onto the mirror and into its eyes
Yes, because cats can see in total darkness without any light
Yes, because mirrors produce their own faint light in dark rooms
No, because mirrors stop reflecting light when nobody is looking
answer: No, because there is no light source to reflect off the cat onto the mirror and into its eyes

question: An object is placed 20 cm from a torch and 20 cm from a screen. If the torch is moved 10 cm further BACK while the object and screen stay in place, what happens to the shadow size?
options: The shadow becomes smaller because the light source is further from the object
The shadow becomes larger because the total distance increased
The shadow stays the same size because the object did not move
The shadow disappears completely
answer: The shadow becomes smaller because the light source is further from the object

question: A triangular chocolate box (with triangular ends and rectangular sides) is rotated in front of a fixed light source. Which pair of shadow shapes can be projected on the screen?
options: A triangle and a rectangle
A circle and a triangle
A square and a circle
A triangle and a circle
answer: A triangle and a rectangle

question: A torch giving off 1000 units of light is pointed at a screen. Four objects (A, B, C, D) of identical size are placed one at a time between torch and screen. Sensor readings at screen: A = 1000 units, B = 0 units, C = 400 units, D = 850 units. Which object forms the DARKEST shadow?
options: Object B
Object A
Object C
Object D
answer: Object B

question: A light ray from a laser pointer hits a smooth flat mirror at a 45-degree angle. What happens to the light ray after hitting the mirror?
options: It bounces off the mirror in a straight line at an equal angle
It stops completely at the mirror surface and turns into a shadow
It scatters randomly in all directions because mirrors bend light
It passes straight through the mirror without changing direction
answer: It bounces off the mirror in a straight line at an equal angle

question: During a shadow puppet performance, an actor wants a dragon puppet's shadow to cover the ENTIRE screen. What two adjustments should be made without changing light brightness?
options: Move torch closer to puppet, and move screen further from puppet
Move torch further from puppet, and move screen closer to puppet
Move puppet closer to screen, and move torch further from screen
Move torch and puppet together closer to the screen
answer: Move torch closer to puppet, and move screen further from puppet

question: Three square sheets (M1, M2, M3) are lined up between a torch and a screen. M1 is transparent glass, M2 is translucent tracing paper, and M3 is opaque cardboard. In which order should they be arranged from torch to screen so that M3 receives light, but NO light reaches the screen?
options: Torch -> M1 -> M2 -> M3 -> Screen
Torch -> M3 -> M2 -> M1 -> Screen
Torch -> M2 -> M3 -> M1 -> Screen
Torch -> M1 -> M3 -> M2 -> Screen
answer: Torch -> M1 -> M2 -> M3 -> Screen

question: An object casts a CIRCULAR shadow on the wall when light shines from the top, and a RECTANGULAR shadow when light shines from the side. Which everyday object could this be?
options: An unopened soup can
A basketball
A party hat
A Rubik's cube
answer: An unopened soup can

question: An object casts a CIRCULAR shadow on the table when light shines from the bottom, and a TRIANGULAR shadow on the wall when light shines from the side. Which everyday object could this be?
options: A party hat
An unopened soup can
A tennis ball
A wooden dice
answer: A party hat
